prose:
Orchestrator ask, 2026-11-12: test_sail_queues_the_ticket_at_codemothers_gates.py failed two teeth on Windows (test_draft_writes_each_stage_without_claim_or_refs and test_verdict_drafts_every_criterion_and_queues_at_the_verdict_gate) with IllegalTransition 'the ticket's serialisation cannot be reproduced', but is 8/8 on Linux. The cause is the proof's fixture, not the door: the proof writes its plan and state files with Path.write_text(json.dumps(...)), which on Windows turns each newline into CRLF, so the ticket file the door reads is CRLF and its round-trip check refuses. The door is clean: artifact._atomic_write writes bytes (tmp.write_bytes), and ticket_file.write_ticket goes through door.write. Measured 2026-11-12 in a scratch clone with the .py eol pin: with newline='
' on the four fixture writes (lines 102, 105, 288, 292) the proof is 8/8 on Windows; unchanged it is 6/8 in both a CRLF and an LF-pinned checkout, so the source eol is not the cause. Census: this fixture shape is common. 298 proof files hold 1163 write_text calls, 496 of them write_text(json.dumps(...)); production code holds 50 write_text calls. Only this proof is in scope here; the rest are named as a census, not fixed.
